concept.title: Vector information versus magnitude-only information
concept.inferential_jump: Equal magnitude alone does not determine a vector because direction is part of the quantity.
entry_assumptions: Can compare ordinary nonnegative sizes and recognise that an arrow has an orientation.

teaching_path.action: Place two equal-length arrows from the same start, one pointing east and one west.
teaching_path.why_valid: Holding the drawn length fixed isolates direction as the only changed feature.
teaching_path.output: Two arrows with the same magnitude and opposite directions.

teaching_path.action: State the magnitude of each arrow, then state the direction of each arrow separately.
teaching_path.why_valid: Magnitude answers only how large; the direction statement carries information the shared magnitude does not.
teaching_path.output: Both magnitudes are equal, but the vectors are different because their directions differ.

teaching_path.action: Reverse one arrow without changing its length and check which description changes.
teaching_path.why_valid: A pure reversal preserves magnitude while changing the vector, directly testing whether magnitude alone identifies the directed quantity.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Two directed quantities with the same magnitude are the same vector.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Two arrows are both 5 units long, one east and one west. Are they the same vector?
misconceptions.repair: Keep the length fixed and compare direction. Equal magnitude does not make two oppositely directed quantities the same vector.

exit_task.prompt: Two arrows have equal length. One points north and the other south. State what is the same, what is different, and whether they are the same vector.

answer.summary: They have the same magnitude but opposite directions, so they are not the same vector.
reasoning: The equal arrow lengths represent equal magnitude.
North and south are different directions.
A vector is identified by magnitude together with direction, so equal magnitude alone is insufficient.
answer.check: Reverse the south-pointing arrow without changing its length; it can then match the north-pointing vector.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The task checks the vector-versus-magnitude distinction without requiring component arithmetic.
